title: Turning an IIS into a planner message

questions.heading: A Planner Message Names Rules and Projects, Never Rows
questions.stem: An IIS holds the row cap_2028 with bound 6,000. The scenario set 2028 at 6,000; the base figure is 8,120. Which sentence belongs in the planner message?

options.text: cap_2028 binds at 6,000 against a base of 8,120 here.
options.says: A row name means nothing to a planner, and 'binding' is model language.

options.text: The 2028 budget row's upper bound is 6,000 (base 8,120).
options.says: Still model language, and it hides who set the number.
Right: plain words, money in $k, and who set the number.

options.text: Raise cap_2028 from 6,000 to 8,120 to make the model feasible.
options.says: A row name again, and ending one conflict need not give a plan.

questions.heading: Show the Arithmetic: Every Way to Start the Projects, and Where It Runs Out
questions.stem: A conflict requires job A (cost 500, in 2027 or 2028) and job B (cost 400, fixed to 2027). The 2027 budget is 600 and the 2028 budget is 300. What does the arithmetic show?

options.text: A in 2027 fits, so the conflict finder made a mistake
options.says: A and B together spend 900 in 2027, against 600.

options.text: Both choices overrun, the closer one by 200 in 2028
options.says: Right: A in 2027 misses by 300; A in 2028 spends 500 against 300, a miss of 200.

options.text: Both choices overrun, the closer one by 300 in 2027
options.says: 300 is the miss when A goes in 2027; moving A to 2028 misses by less.

options.text: A in 2028 fits, so only job B needs to move a year

questions.heading: Each Conflict Ends With the Changes That End It, in the Planners' Words
questions.stem: A message lists two conflicts. Raising the 2028 budget would end the first. A planner raises it and reruns, and the model is still infeasible. Why?

options.text: The message was wrong, since ending one conflict always gives a plan
options.says: An IIS's way out ends that conflict only; others can remain.

options.text: The solver is unstable, since the same scenario changed its answer
options.says: The scenario changed (a higher budget), and the answer is still a proof.

options.text: The budget row was hard, so raising its bound changed nothing
options.says: Raising the bound did end the first conflict; another remains.

options.text: Another conflict remains, since ending one need not give a plan
options.says: Right: the lesson's message lists every conflict, then one repair checked by a solve.
